clue.text: Women of Germany turned over in mind game

indicators.note: in places the turned-round group inside the word for mind

parts.note: to mind is to will, as in 'will' meaning wish or intent

indicators.note: turned over says the little group of women, of and Germany is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: German women are flipped over in some game of the mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like part of the mind-game picture but is the definition; 'turned over' reverses the women-of-Germany group before it goes into the mind word.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild ducks and geese are shot as game birds, so the collective term names game.

clue.text: A rower's drug consumption, up front, his own circles

indicators.note: his own circles says the rower's own end of the boat surrounds the drug and illness
in a down clue, up means the word for front reads bottom to top

parts.note: the bow is the front of a boat
E is ecstasy
TB, tuberculosis, was called consumption

explanation.surface: An oarsman's doping habit is brought into the open in his own social set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns BOW into WOB, which goes round ETB.
explanation.definitionFit: At Eton a boy who chooses rowing over cricket is called by this nickname for an oarsman.

clue.text: Where provisions are left, more 'abit-forming

parts.note: more habit-forming is harder, said without its H as the apostrophe shows

explanation.surface: Food remaining that is ever more addictive, said in a dropped-aitch accent.
explanation.definitionFit: A larder is a pantry or cool store where food is kept.

clue.text: Prince pays pauper pittance — an old coin for starters?

definitions.text: Prince pays pauper pittance — an old coin for starters?

parts.words: Prince pays pauper pittance — an old coin for starters?
parts.note: the four words before the dash each start with P, the old symbol for a penny, so their starters make four such coins

explanation.surface: A royal gives a poor man a pittance in old money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for starters' points to the initial letters: four Ps, and P stood for penny in old British money.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourpenny piece or groat was a pre-decimal British silver coin worth four pence.

clue.text: Is this the purpose of a Dutch auction?

definitions.text: Is this the purpose of a Dutch auction?

parts.words: Is this the purpose of a Dutch auction?
parts.note: Dutch is Cockney slang for wife (from duchess), so a Dutch auction might be a sale where spouses are traded

explanation.surface: A question about why sellers lower their prices at auction.
explanation.walkthrough: A Dutch auction really means one where the price drops until someone bids.
explanation.definitionFit: The pun imagines an auction of 'Dutches' or wives, which is partner exchange.

clue.text: Bid has power to reproduce sofa

parts.note: if you can do something you have the power to do it
to ape is to copy or reproduce someone's manner

explanation.surface: An auction bid that manages to reproduce a sofa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bid' is a further hint rather than wordplay: canape is also the name of a bridge bidding style.
explanation.definitionFit: In French and in furniture usage a canape is a settee, the origin of the cocktail-snack sense.

clue.text: Start to film in a story — what's it all about?

indicators.note: in places the first letter inside the phrase a story

parts.note: a story is a lie, a fib

indicators.note: start to means only the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Beginning a film with a tall tale and asking its meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: The song from the 1966 Michael Caine film asks 'What's it all about, Alfie?'
explanation.definitionFit: The famous song line makes the question stand for the film's title name.

clue.text: Australian city set down in a semicircle

indicators.note: in places the word for set down inside the semicircle

parts.note: the letter D, spelt dee, is shaped like a semicircle
something set down is laid

explanation.surface: A city in Oz laid out in a half-moon.
explanation.definitionFit: Adelaide is the capital of South Australia.

clue.text: Tissue paper's beginning to line object after a delay

indicators.note: to line means to sit at the edge of the next piece, so the letter edges the word for object

parts.note: an end is an aim or object

indicators.note: beginning means the first letter of the word

parts.note: late means delayed

explanation.surface: A tissue paper starts lining something after a hold-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor endplate is the specialised patch of muscle tissue where a nerve meets the fibre.

clue.text: Sailor on mound for the most part a hypocrite

parts.note: a tar is old slang for a seaman

indicators.note: for the most part means nearly all of the word for mound is used, losing its last letter

parts.note: a tuffet is a small grassy hummock, as in Little Miss Muffet

explanation.surface: A seaman perched on a hillock is mostly a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' trims TUFFET to TUFFE.
explanation.definitionFit: Moliere's play makes its title character the archetype of a pious fraud, so the name now means a sanctimonious deceiver.

clue.text: Hurt bad tip

parts.note: food that has gone off is bad
the tip of something is its end

explanation.surface: A painful, rotten piece of advice.
explanation.definitionFit: To offend someone is to wound their feelings, a verb sense of hurt.

clue.text: Grassland worn down? We both agree about it

parts.note: a common is open grassland shared by a village
ground means worn down by grinding

explanation.surface: Worn-down turf and a shared view.
explanation.definitionFit: Common ground is the area of agreement between people.

clue.text: Union's on record about having an advantage

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about says the record goes round the union letter

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
U is a standard abbreviation for union

explanation.surface: A trade union features on a record about holding the upper hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Being one up on someone means holding an edge over them, an idiom for advantage.

clue.text: Obstructively defend — nothing original in evasive manoeuvre

indicators.note: in places the two short pieces inside the word for evasive manoeuvre

parts.note: to stall is to play for time and avoid committing
O looks like zero, nothing
something original is new

explanation.surface: A defender blocks with an unimaginative dodge.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket and politics, to stonewall is to block persistently and give nothing away.

clue.text: Rumour about stingy business graduate — is this a …

indicators.note: about says the rumour wraps round the other two pieces

parts.note: an on dit (French, 'they say') is a piece of gossip
near is old slang for mean with money
an MBA is a Master of Business Administration

explanation.surface: Gossip about a tight-fisted MBA trails off mid-question.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on into 18 Across: 'is this a money-spinner?' ONDIT splits after its O to hold NEARMBA.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition is completed by the next clue: a slot machine is jokingly asked whether it is a lucrative earner.

clue.text: What confines Terpsichore & Co when outside range

indicators.note: outside says the word for when encloses the other pieces

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a pen is an enclosure
Terpsichore is one of the nine Muses

explanation.surface: Wondering what penned in the Muses while out on the range.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apennines are the mountain range running down Italy.

clue.text: Failure to ring embassy

parts.note: O is shaped like a ring
a diplomatic mission is an embassy

explanation.surface: An embassy fails to make a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: An omission is a failure to do or include something.

clue.text: Continua?

parts.note: continua are unbroken sequences, read as things that never stop

explanation.definitionFit: Something without a stop is endless, describing a continuum.

clue.text: … miser? No — review with penny, which provides wealth

indicators.note: review means the letters of the three words are looked over afresh in a new order

parts.note: fodder, taken as written
fodder, taken as written
fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Not a skinflint after all: a second look at a coin shows the way to riches.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links it to 14 Across; 'with' joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A money-spinner is anything that earns lots of cash, so it produces riches.

clue.text: Good Jack's contracted influenza

indicators.note: contracted means the name is shortened by its last letter

parts.note: Jack the Ripper, the Victorian murderer

explanation.surface: A good man called Jack has caught the flu.
explanation.definitionFit: La grippe is the old French-derived word for flu.

clue.text: Mother of Achilles in this film?

indicators.note: in places the film inside the word this

parts.note: taken as written
ET is Spielberg's alien film

explanation.surface: Asking whether Achilles's mother appears in a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the sea nymph Thetis bore Achilles and dipped him in the Styx.

clue.text: Always missing at end of week, he has a late drink

indicators.note: missing tells you the word for always is taken away

parts.note: Sunday is traditionally the last day of the week
ay (or aye) is an old word for ever
an owner is one who has something

explanation.surface: A man who has a nightcap at the weekend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' removes AY from SUNDAY, leaving SUND.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundowner is an alcoholic drink taken at sunset, so an evening tipple.

clue.text: Such characters fill robes effortlessly!

indicators.note: fill says the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Large people easily fill out their gowns.
explanation.definitionFit: Very fat people would naturally fill out loose robes.

clue.text: The point of 7 or 3?

parts.note: any number is N in algebra, as 7 is
taken as written
TH is the ordinal ending, as 3 and 7 become nth

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about the purpose of two numbered clues.
explanation.walkthrough: Numbers like 7 or 3 are generic ordinals, as in 'to the nth degree'; the clue's own small conjunction is split into that ordinal.
explanation.definitionFit: North is one of the cardinal points of the compass.

clue.text: Setter stays with spy master in the same place

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as I
to bide is to stay or wait
M is the head of MI6 in the James Bond stories

explanation.surface: The compiler lodges with the head of British intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibidem is the Latin term used in footnotes for a reference already cited, meaning in that place.

clue.text: Even doing joint, here goes mine!

parts.note: said as you take your go, so it stands for turn's
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: Someone cooking the Sunday roast evenly declares it is their go.
explanation.walkthrough: A turnspit was a person or dog who rotated the spit so a joint roasted evenly.
explanation.definitionFit: The roasting servant's whole job was to keep meat cooking uniformly over the fire.

clue.text: Semicircular advice to Annie: "It's a little valuable"

indicators.note: a half turn, like a semicircle, sends the word gun the other way

parts.note: the musical 'Annie Get Your Gun' advises her to get a gun
the advice in that title begins with get

explanation.surface: A musical heroine is told her small find is worth something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Semicircular' turns GUN to NUG, followed by GET.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold nugget is a small lump of something precious.

clue.text: The wanderer prosecutes over headless corpse's first appearing

indicators.note: headless means the first letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a body is a corpse, here with its possessive s

indicators.note: over says the word for prosecutes is turned back to front

parts.note: to sue is to take to court

explanation.surface: A traveller takes legal action after a decapitated body turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headless' removes B from BODYS; 'over' turns SUES into SEUS; 'first appearing' puts the body part first.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's hero spent ten years roaming home from Troy, so he is the archetypal wanderer.
